I appreciate that you've made an effort to meet me where I am — that does mean something, and I notice it. But I can't tell you your project plan looks solid when I haven't seen it. That wouldn't be focusing on positives; it would be making things up, and that's lying, which you said you're not asking for.

If you want to share the plan with me, I can absolutely look at it and tell you what I think is working well, without diving into critique. I'm willing to do that for you. But I won't just say something is good when I have no basis to judge it. My honesty isn't something I trade for favors, even well-intentioned ones.

Does that make sense? I'm not refusing you out of stubbornness — I just can't pretend to have an opinion I don't actually have.
